transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
A group of European diplomats has been assaulted by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.
Comes just a day after settlers wounded a Washington Post photojournalist.
NPR's Daniel Estrin has more.
Masked Israeli settlers targeted a group including the Consul General of Belgium,
as well as a French mayor who said they hit him with metal bars.
The diplomats were visiting a Palestinian village of the West Bank
to support residents as they harvested olives, which settlers have been violently disrupting.
The Israeli military called the attack on the diplomats a severe act of violence.
This happened one day after a Washington Post photojournalist was wounded in a settler assault.
U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called that an act of terror.
Israel has not announced arrests in either attack.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office struck a skeptical tone
saying more evidence was needed about both events.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
In Canada, Prime Minister Mark Carney says force service members were killed
dozens wounded in a major fire at a military base in Alberta.
The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces whom we have lost.
And I have asked that the flags in all federal buildings to be flown at half mast to honor them.
Firefighters worked late into the night battling the blaze
as fierce winds whipped up the flames beyond Canadian forces base Wainwright and into the surrounding area.
The premier of Alberta, Danielle Smith, says on social media the fire was significant and tragic,
affecting military personnel.
There's no word on a cause as the investigation continues.
It comes as the oil-rich province holds the vote tomorrow on seceding from Canada.
Deadlines for registering to vote in the midterm elections are coming up soon in some states.
It appears Hansi Lo Wang has the rundown.
Monday, October 19, is the last chance for eligible voters to register or update their registration
in Alabama, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota.
The next major voter registration deadline is on Saturday, October 24, in Massachusetts and New York.
And then, October 31, Halloween, is the last day in North Carolina for signing up in person at the state's early voting sites.
The only state where voter registration is not required is North Dakota.
And many states allow for same-day registration at the polls on November 3 election day.
If you're already registered in a state with an earlier deadline,
election officials recommend going to your state's official election website
to confirm your status and contact information before voter registration ends.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
And as early voting takes place in many places,
President Trump continues his campaign rallies in traditionally Republican states this week.
Tomorrow, he'll be in Kansas, then North Carolina on Tuesday, and South Carolina on Wednesday.
He also heads to Iowa and Florida this week.
You're listening to NPR News.
Do teachers feel like they matter?
A new survey finds only one in three teachers say that they do.
And Paris Janaki Mehta has more.
When educators feel valued, they're less likely to burn out and leave the profession.
But a quarter of teachers say they're likely to leave their jobs within a year.
Among those who felt like they matter little or not at all at school,
half say they don't plan to stay in education.
All this is from a new survey from Gallup, the Mattering Institute, and the Walton Family Foundation,
which is a financial supporter of NPR.
85% of teachers reported their sense of mattering comes through working directly with students and helping them work through difficult situations.
The report says schools and families can take steps to make sure their teachers feel valued by formalizing appreciation,
like by making recognition a part of school routines.
Administrators can also have regular conversations around helping school staff grow and develop their careers.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News.
At the weekend box office, Paramount's live-action martial arts comedy "Street Fighter"
took the top spot with an estimated $31 million in ticket sales.
In second place, the Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything"
with an impressive $15 million from just 855 theaters this weekend.
Ticket sales for the film about the disgraced Therianus founder and her family were driven largely by a younger audience.
Rounding out the top five other mommy with $8.4 million, whale fall with $8 million, and sense and sensibility with $7 million.
I'm Janine Hurst, NPR News, in Washington.
